Introduction
From time to time, some institutions strive for breaking monotony which may
befall their plans and projects, and accordingly tend to the refurbishment of
executive mechanisms, introduce new ideas and methods for the project subject
of renovation, or invent slogans and denominations which shall have impact on
the morale of its executing personnel as well as its beneficiaries, which draw
attention of people, fill them with enthusiasm and materialize the idea into
reality with a new dimension.
Inspired by this, the United Nations went ahead to boost its programs in the field
of development and youth welfare when it proposed the idea of the International
Youth Year and declared three axes that required to intensify the efforts
thereby, namely Participation, Development & Peace, as these axes are implicitly
existing under the goals behind establishment of the United Nations and they are
materialized through various programs running under the auspices of the United
Nations, and these goals were again introduced in the above manner in order to
lend the idea a new dimension and enthuse an innovative spirit in youth so they
can reach a more vital level of participation. The General Assembly adopted two
Resolutions i.e. No. 34/151 dated 17 December 1979 and No. 35/126 dated
11December 1980 stating that the Year 1985 shall be named as the International
Youth Year under the slogan of “Participation, Development & Peace”. Following
these resolutions, international, continental and regional consultative committees
were formed, preliminary and follow-up meetings were held to implement the
recommendations issued by these committees, and execute plans and programs
which were approved with the purpose of participation in the efforts aimed to
achieve the goals of the International youth Year.
The GCC Countries were among those countries which were very keen to
participate in these meetings and take positive initiatives towards this trend. The
GCC Secretariat General took part in the meeting which was held by the
Economic Committee for West Asia in Baghdad in which the regional action
plan in West Asia was approved for the International Youth Year. The action
plan consisted of twenty eight pages which was of great interest for the youth
and sports bodies in the GCC Countries upon laying down its own planning.

Since the participation is among the important principles of the social work and
while the development is a combination of manpower and environmental
resources, and their interaction helps to achieve welfare for a man or fulfill his
increasingly new requirements so that he can serve humanity by promoting
stability, peace and cooperation with his fellow brethren. The participation or
development can not be achieved in absence of peace which is the result of the
participation and development. The United Nations combined these three powers
in a single track to face the problems which threaten the man and his
environment. The youth are common factors to boost this trend as they are
concerned with this project and because they are vital elements in this stage, they
will carry on the responsibilities of the future.
Henceforth, the trend of the United Nations was sharp and active and inspiring
for playing the role in human responsibilities, due to which it is a must to
welcome the International Youth Year and extend all possible support in order
to materialize its goals and put up initiatives which aim at materializing those
goals into reality.
Following the goals laid by Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf
and inspired by its role towards the man , environment and society, the GCC
Secretariat General is taking up the joint action in this filed, and is presenting
this publication which consists of most important achievements of the GCC
Countries in the filed of youth and sports activities on the occasion of the
International Youth Year, and feels proud of achievements of the GCC
Countries during the first decade of the International Youth Year, whether it
was at the local level of each state or combined platform of the GCC Countries
or their participation at the international level. Moreover, it appreciates that the
United Nations takes care of the youth and draws people’s attention to their care
and exploitation of their energies for participation, development and peace.
The Secretariat General hopes that this documentary pamphlet will be beneficial
in enriching the experience, and that its efforts will be combined with the efforts
of other countries so that this publication may serve as a reference to upcoming
generations. In the end, The Secretariat General would like to point out that
there are many achievements to its credit which could not find place in this
report, as they were implemented by other authorities such as Ministries of
Education and Ministries of Social Affairs etc. while this report concentrates on
prominent efforts exerted by the youth and sports bodies.
The Secretariat General
Philosophy of youth and sports activities in the GCC Countries
The youth and sports bodies in the GCC Countries are following a
comprehensive method regarding youth welfare and sports, as they view their
institutions as they are educational institutions in a comprehensive sense of
education (physical, mental and spiritual) and any other bodies and institutions
which take part in forming the personality of a good citizen.

At this point, we find that most of the youth and sports institutions in the GCC
Countries carry out sports, cultural, social and scientific activities, because the
nature of the social life in the GCC Countries requires this trend, but the
comprehensiveness did not come in the way of independent specialized
institutions like specialized Scientific Centers as well as professional, literary and
cultural clubs.
The purpose of these institutions is to meet requirements of the youth as well as
of man in general, in the field of developing his tendencies, boosting his talents,
providing him with knowledge, building his physique, enhancing his thinking,
and exploiting his energies for the service of his society, his environment and his
fellow countrymen. Moreover these institutions are trying to instill a sense of
citizenship and confidence in its members and its visitors.
A number of awareness campaigns were organized following beneficial methods
for the man, and warning people of dangers befalling the society like
indifference, non-cooperation, negligence and narcotics etc.. which damage the
society and health of man. Further, they are concerned with the institutional as
well as rectifying studies on which the work is based and is tested.
This trend confirms the achievements and programs which are observed by a
common person and are confirmed by the resolution issued in the Second
Meeting of the Youth Welfare & Sports Ministers. The Resolution issued in the
Second Meeting of Heads of the Olympic Committees at the GCC Countries,
which is considered a youth & sports document, defined the most important
foundations and outsets on which this activity is based on:
1. Youth welfare which means educational, spiritual,
physical and comprehensive training gained through
sponsoring cultural, social, sports and scientific activities
etc. which develop the personality of the young and
provide them with a field in which they can express their
opinion and;
2. Noble principles of sports which concentrate on physical
training and development of good relations among
different societies and participants in sports activities,
respect for others and for their achievements.
3. Olympic Covenant which contains principles and trends
of the Olympic movement.
4. International youth and sports activities in accordance
with membership of the GCC Countries in the Arabian,
Continental and International organizations, abiding by
the agreements and laws and regulations governing such
activities and their relations with other countries.
5. Scout activities, their educational principles and ethics in
developing the skills, hobbies, service to the environment
and society.
6. Human solidarity with peace loving societies and nations
in order to participate in achieving peace, development,

mutual closeness and cooperation.
7. Citizens’ participation is one of the principles of the social
work in order to achieve integrity between public and
private sectors with an emphasis on the citizenship and
participation in the development.
Should we look at these foundations and principles, we shall find that they
harmonize with the spirit of the trends of the Year, and this is what makes
dealing with those trends by the said authorities an easily adjusting and
implementing matter because of their harmony with the activities of the youth
and sports institutions.
The following sectors in the GCC Countries are responsible for the youth sports
affairs :
- Ministries of Education
- Ministries of Higher Education
- Ministries of Defense
- Ministries of Interior
Including all the students and scholars belonging to them.
Also, the private sector pays attention to the youth activities for its employees
and staff who have their own clubs and centers which organize sports, cultural
and social activities for them.
As for direct responsibility for youth and sports, it rests with youth and sports
bodies and Olympic committees and their ancillary commissions, committees,
unions, clubs, centers and associations. These bodies are:
- Ministry of Education & Youth Affairs in the United Arab Emirates.
- General Organization for youth & sports in the State of Bahrain.
- General Presidency for Youth Welfare in the Kingdom of Saudi
Arabia.
- General Board for Youth, Sports & Cultural Activities in the Sultanate
of Oman.
- General Board for Youth & Sports in the State of Qatar.
- General Board for Youth & Sports in the State of Kuwait.
There are several associations and scout bodies which take care of youth and
juniors training.
The joint action in the field of youth and sports emphasizes the participation by
the youth in chalking out the plans to aim at youth activities. Consequently,
committees were formed to study youth affairs and to lay the plans which
respond to achieve their expectations and aspirations, and deal with the
problems and issues concerning them.

Achievements
in the Field of International Youth Year Trends
The GCC Countries concerned themselves with the resolution of the United
Nations relating to declaration of the International Youth Year in which the UN
invited all countries to concentrate on activities that should infuse in the youth a
participation spirit, method of development and peace, and make them
participate in making the plans that will fulfill their expectations and utilize their
experience with the purpose of boosting this sector making it contribute to the
service of humanity, development of the society and promotion of peace, through
three axes (Participation, Development & Peace) the slogan of the International
Youth Year and called for adoption of its goals and take practical initiatives. The
activities of the GCC Countries are concentrated on the following lines:
First : On the local level of the GCC Countries
Second : On the International level of the GCC Countries
Third : On the joint level of the GCC Countries
Fourth : On the joint International level of the GCC Countries
The Detail is given in the following pages:
First : The local level of the GCC Countries
As we explained earlier when we referred to the philosophy of the youth and
sports activities in the GCC Countries that their goal is to mould the personality
of an individual and inspire him to participate in those activities so that his
contribution can be active and beneficial for himself, his country and mankind.
The GCC Countries welcomed the United Nations’ declaration of the
International Youth Year and showed readiness to participate in adopting the
Year’s goals and supporting the activities and initiatives leading to success.
The GCC Countries marched forward to take part in the international,
continental and regional conferences which were organized to make the concept
of the International Youth Year popular, and formed local committees in each
state from the ministries and authorities concerned with youth affairs,
educational, training, development and social work. They also formed a
committee for the International youth Year in which all the GCC Countries took
part at the level of a department manager to follow the joint works and activities
approved for this occasion and coordinate and exchange experiences of each
country regarding the activities carried out by each country.
After a number of meetings of local committees, local plans were approved
which were financed by youth and sports authorities and private sector in each
GCC Country. Schedule (1) shows some implementations of these plans :

Second : On the International level of the GCC Countries
The GCC Countries are keen to take part in the International activities –
regional, continental, and international, because the purpose of these activities is
to bring people closer and promote cooperation among them, as well as to
remove barriers, break segregation and strengthen human ties so the peace and
understanding may prevail in order to make the problems diminish and facilitate
their solutions. The GCC Countries are also keen to take membership in the
International organizations and bodies to work shoulder to shoulder with the
international community for achieving active participation, development and
peace. On this track, wefind ththe GCCountries have been participating in the
activities which were organized on the International level in the field of
International Youth Year and participated therein apart from the joint action
plan. These activities are explained in Schedule (2) which describes the

Third : On the joint level of the GCC Countries
On the joint level, the work started with formation of a joint committee
“International Youth Year Committee” in which all member countries
participated on the level of department director. The committee kept on its
meetings and drew its plans to welcome the first decade of the International
Youth Year (1985-1995), and follow up its to activities and to celebrate its tenth
anniversary. Then it authorized the specialized committees to implement those
activities. Those committees include “social, cultural, scientific, scout and sports
committees”. Among the resolutions passed by the committees, are the following
:
1. Design a logo for the International Youth Year in the GCC Countries.
2. Conduct a rectifying study for the youth & sports institutions in the
GCC Countries in order to know the extent of benefiting from the
institutions and introduce something new to their services.
3. Conduct a study for folklore games and include them in sports,
recreational and competitive activities.
4. Conduct a study for childhood services in the GCC Countries and
develop their institutions.
5. Conduct local studies for issues concerning the youth and problems
facing them, and proposing solutions for such problems.
6. Issue a documentary booklet on the efforts exerted by the GCC
Countries in the way of achieving goals of the International Youth
Year.
7. Celebrating the first decade of the International Youth Year.
8. Celebrating the first anniversary of the first decade of the
International Youth Year.
9. Carry out cultural, scientific, social and sports activities.
10. Hold training courses, symposiums and dialogues.
11. Exchange visits with different countries in the world.
12. Construction of youth and sports institutions.
13. Provide financial aid to the youth and sports institutions, their
programs and activities.
14. Take initiatives on local and collective levels to develop the youth
and sports activities.
15. Highlight the goals of International Youth Year through youth and
sports bodies and means of communications in each country over the
first decade.
16. Implement periodic joint activities. Schedule (3) explains the
achievements of these plans.
17. Provide opportunity to the expatriates residing in the GCC Countries
so that they can pursue their sports, cultural and social activities in
the youth and sports institutions.

sports institutions, arrangement of meetings with youth therein, work shops for

technical meets, competitions in cultural and scientific activities such as
inventions, researches and photography.
These activities are managed by the specialized joint committees which hold its
meetings periodically, set forth implementing conceptions and organizational
rules and regulations, recommend incentives and souvenirs, and rectify the
experiments and input modifications to the activities.
The joint activities have a positive role in improving the local activities in order
to achieve inter-active or distinguishing participation which in turn improve the
performance of those institutions.
The first decade of the International Youth is received as follows :
1. Speech of His Excellency the Secretary General in which he praised the
idea, and urged the communication media and youth & sports authorities to give
attention to the trends of International Youth Yeand to oyouth actin this regard.
2. Media meetings with the senior officials of the International Youth Year
in the GCC Countries and explain its goals, role of the public and private
sectors for participation.
Fourth : On the joint International level of the GCC Countries
In line with the trends of the International Youth Year and for achieving its
goals, the joint action was concerned with the contact with the international
community. Two communications channels were established with the
international communities. The first channel is concerned with improvement of
the relations with the developing countries and for which activity camps were
assigned that aim at environmental services and society development. Out of
which four camps were organized in Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Egypt which
were arranged in rural areas selected by the host countries responsible for
establishment of those camps. Each camp included 60 young men from the GCC
Countries while other sixty youth belonged to the host country. These camps
were supervised by responsible authorities from host countries, the GCC
Countries and the Secretariat General. Moreover, those camps were financed by
the GCC Countries shared by the host countries and GCC Secretariat General.
The camps erected a number of educational and youth buildings, and water
tanks which were linked with the alleys. Besides, thousands of trees were planted
and long agricultural and rural roads were paved, in addition to renovation of
the schools and health utilities. Youth training courses were conducted in the
host country and many cultural, social and sports activities including awareness
programs were implemented. Those camps were highly welcomed by the host
countries with their cooperation extended, and they opened doors for the
voluntary service.
The second channel consisted of cultural festivals, technical and scientific
exhibitions. Social, sports and scout meetings were held and organized. A great
cultural festival was held in Japan and an exhibition in Paris displaying the
scientific inventions of the youth

of the GCC Countries. Sports tournaments were held each in Japan and China,
and social and scout visits were made to Germany and China. The GCC
Countries also received artistic and sports delegations from a number of peace
loving countries. During those meetings, spirit of much sought human solidarity
prevailed and the delegations embodied the principles and trends of the
International Youth Year.
Among the above delegations, a Japanese delegation was received which visited
around the GCC Countries, along with sports teams in Football, Judo & Karate.
A Japanese Musical Team, an administrative delegation from Peoples Republic
of China, and a Japanese Parliamentary Delegation from Japan’s Friendship
Association also arrived .
A group of scientific clubs took part in the camps which were organized in
France and Tunisia with scientific and diving campaigns in Jordan and Egypt.

- Celebration of the tenth anniversary of the International Youth Year:
While celebrating the tenth anniversary of the
International Youth Year and pursuant to the resolutions

of the youth welfare and sports Ministers, the following
activities were conducted:
- Symposiums were organized locally on Voluntary Work
and its impact on development of social activities in the
field of youth activities, and make people aware of the
goals and trends of the International Youth Year.
- Hold a photo exhibition and a symposium on the goals of
the International Youth Year and achievements of the
GCC Countries in this filed participated by all the GCC
Countries.
- Intensify the social activities specially in the field of goals
of International Youth Year (namely Participation,
Development & Peace), highlighting their goals, and
issuing brochures which should explain the goals of the
International Youth Year.
- Documentation of these activities and providing the
Secretariat General with their photos and description so
they can be included in the brochure issued by the
Secretariat General on this occasion.
- A football tournament was organized whose revenues
were collected for the sake of UNICEF.
Fourth:
Ministers of youth and sports issued a statement at the beginning of 1996 about
the International Youth Year. Its text reads as follows:
Statement of Ministers of Youth & Sports
Of CooperaCouncil for the Arab States of the Gulf
On the occasion of the Tenth Anniversary of
the International Youth Year
The Ministers of Youth & Sports of Cooperation Council for the Arab States of
the Gulf while celebrating the Tenth Anniversary of the International Youth
Year, express their appreciation for the efforts exerted by the youth and sports
organizations and other national institutions in the GCC Countries towards
materializing the trends of the International Youth Year (Participation,
Development & Peace), and praise the achievements attained in this field on the
local level for each state as well as on the joint level of the GCC Countries.
Keeping in mind the membership of their countries in the International
Organization, the ministers realize the common responsibility entrusted with the
international community, and its governmental as well as private institutions to
achieve the goals of the International Youth Year which aim at embodying the
collective participation in order to achieve comprehensive developments, spread
peace and bring people of the globe closer and closer.
The ministers confirm their determination to carry on a serious pursuit and
active continuity to support youth activities which shall attain

comprehensiveness in youth care, respond to the trends which shall be beneficial
for them and their countries, and deepen the relations between their societies
and other communities, in compliance with their true religion – Islam – and
trends of their institutions, and they shall exert their best efforts to assist the
international community to keep up its best efforts to achieve the goals and
trends of the International Youth Year, through the programs and plans put
forth by the youth and sports institutions in the GCC Countries on the local,
joint and international levels.
The ministers, while confirming their determination to intensify the efforts in
this field, do not have doubt that the international community shall pursue the
same efforts to support these trends, establish cooperation and coordination
among its institutions to intensify good efforts and remove barriers and factors
of difference among the nations.
The ministers take this opportunity to invite the international community to
extend help to the developing countries and support their youth and educational
institutions materially and technically, and appeal to the concerned international
institutions to increase degree of awareness regarding dangers of narcotics,
terrorism, and outlets of deviation, demanding opening new horizons of
activities, work fields and production for the youth to wisely utilize their spare
time and save their countries from any harm. The ministers while issuing this
statement, declare their solidarity with the efforts exerted for care of the young
generation and strengthen their ties with their countries and assimilation with
their fellow partners in the world.
Wishing good luck for all.
